key_insight: Small initialization can create a nonmonotone "accuracy well": accuracy rises early, drops later due to a bottleneck, then recovers after further optimization.
engineering_relevance: For training and deployment, monitoring accuracy over time can reveal failure modes that loss alone hides, especially in deep models initialized near zero.
method: Analyze training dynamics under vanishing initialization.
Study deep linear, ReLU, and convolutional models on synthetic and benchmark classification tasks.
Build a staged explanation: target-driven organization, degeneracy bottleneck, and later recruitment/recovery.
evidence_signal: The phenomenon is observed in training and test accuracy across deep linear networks, fully connected ReLU networks on MNIST, deep CNNs on CIFAR-10, and controlled synthetic tasks under different losses and optimizers.
watch_item: Early accuracy gains can be misleading; continuing optimization may temporarily worsen classification even when loss changes are asymptotically tiny.
paper_title: The Accuracy Well: Nonmonotone Accuracy Dynamics at Vanishing Initialization
